`injectCoauthor()` in `src/tools/bash.ts` splices the configured co-author name and email into a double-quoted shell argument, so quotes, `$()`, backticks, or `;` in either value run arbitrary commands whenever a git commit goes through the bash tool, and line breaks can forge extra trailers. Make the generated shell static: pass the trailer and the temp message path through environment variables (`KF_COAUTHOR_TRAILER`, `KF_COAUTHOR_MSG`) referenced only as `"$VAR"`, with no `eval`. Add `buildCoauthorTrailer()` that rejects line breaks, control characters, U+2028/U+2029, and `<`/`>` in the email; an invalid value skips injection with a warning while the user's command still runs. The temp message file must be removed whether the amend succeeds or fails. Keep detection of commit-producing commands, rebase continuation, the HEAD-change safety net, duplicate-trailer detection, and non-git behaviour unchanged.

The regression test(s) for this change are already in the worktree: `src/tools/bash.test.ts`. Read them to see the exact API and behaviour expected, then implement the change so they pass. Do not modify the test files; they are restored before verification. Run the tests with `npx tsx --test src/tools/bash.test.ts` and `npm run typecheck` before you finish.
